verses.zh: 以色列人出去与非利士人打仗，安营在以便以谢；非利士人安营在亚弗。
verses.en: Samuel revealed the word of the Lord[NOTE:1] to all Israel.The Ark of the Covenant is Lost to the PhilistinesThen the Israelites went out to fight the Philistines.[NOTE:2] They camped at Ebenezer,[NOTE:3] and the Philistines camped at Aphek.
notes: Heb “and the word of Samuel was.” The present translation understands Samuel to be the speaker of the divine word (“Samuel” is a subjective genitive in this case), although the statement could mean that he was the recipient of the divine word (“Samuel” is an objective genitive in this case) who in turn reported it to Israel.
Heb “and Israel went out to meet the Philistines for battle.”

Heb “the stone, the help.” The second noun is in apposition to the first one and apparently is the name by which the stone was known. Contrast the expression used in 5:1 and 7:12, where the first word lacks the definite article, unlike 4:1.
verses.commentary:
4:1 "the word of Samuel" This was really the word of YHWH (cf. 1 Sam. 3:19-21).

▣ "came to all Israel" This relates to 1 Sam. 3:20 (i.e., "Dan to Beersheba").

▣ "the Philistines" The Philistines were apparently Greeks from the Aegean Islands. They were the only
group of people in this part of the world who were uncircumcised. They were apparently a mercenary force who tried to
attack Egypt in the twelfth century b.c. but were defeated. They then settled on the southern coast of Palestine. They had
five major cities which are delineated in Josh. 13:3 Gaza, Ashdod, Ashkelon, Gath, and Ekron. They were a major military
problem throughout the period of the judges and even throughout the reign of Saul and David. The name "Palestine" comes
from the word "Philistine."

See NIDOTTE, vol. 4, pp. 1048-1052.

▣ "Ebenezer. . .Aphek" See map # 83, p. 68 in The MacMillan Bible Atlas. This location was at the
northern limit of the Philistine territory, near an important pathway from the hill country to the sea coast plain.

verses.zh: 非利士人向以色列人摆阵。两军交战的时候，以色列人败在非利士人面前；非利士人在战场上杀了他们的军兵约有四千人。
verses.en: The Philistines arranged their forces to fight[NOTE:1] Israel. As the battle spread out,[NOTE:2] Israel was defeated by[NOTE:3] the Philistines, who[NOTE:4] killed about 4,000 men in the battle line in the field.
notes: Heb “to meet.”

The MT has וַתִּטֹּשׁ (vattittosh), from the root נָטַשׁ (natash). This verb normally means “to leave,” “to forsake,” or “to permit,” but such an idea does not fit this context very well. Many scholars have suspected that the text originally read either וַתֵּט (vattet, “and it spread out”), from the root נָטָה (natah), or וַתִּקֶשׁ (vattiqesh, “and it grew fierce”), from the root קָשַׂה (qasah). The former suggestion is apparently supported by the LXX ἔκλινεν (eklinen, “it inclined”) and is adopted in the translation.
Heb “before.”

Heb “the Philistines, and they killed.” The pronoun “they” has been translated as a relative pronoun (“who”) to make it clear to the English reader that the Philistines were the ones who did the killing.
verses.commentary:
4:2 "four thousand men" This is obviously a round number. "Thousand" can refer to a military unit but with the
addition of "men," it is just a large round number.

SPECIAL TOPIC: THOUSAND (eleph)

verses.zh: 百姓回到营里，以色列的长老说：「耶和华今日为何使我们败在非利士人面前呢？我们不如将耶和华的约柜从示罗抬到我们这里来，好在我们中间救我们脱离敌人的手。」
verses.en: When the army[NOTE:1] came back to the camp, the elders of Israel said, “Why did the Lord let us be defeated today by[NOTE:2] the Philistines? Let’s take with us the ark of the covenant of the Lord from Shiloh. When it is with us, it will save us[NOTE:3] from the hand of our enemies.”
notes: Or “people.”
Heb “before.”

Heb “and it will come in our midst and it will save.” After the cohortative (see “let’s take”), the prefixed verbal forms with the prefixed conjunction indicate purpose or result. The translation understands the ark to be the subject of the third masculine singular verbs, although it is possible to understand the Lord as the subject. In the latter case, one should translate, “when he is with us, he will save us.”
verses.commentary:
4:3 "elders" See SPECIAL TOPIC: ELDERS

▣ "Why has the Lord defeated us today before the Philistines"This event
can be viewed in several ways.

- The sin of Eli's sons caused the judgment of YHWH to fall on all Israel (i.e., Hebrew corporality, cf. Joshua 7).

- All causality was attributed to YHWH (i.e., no secondary causes); this was a way to assert His sovereignty
(cf. 2 Chr. 20:6; Eccl. 7:14; Isa. 14:24-27; 43:13; 45:7; 54:16; Jer. 18:11; Lam. 3:33-38; Amos 3:6).

- YHWH was revealing His characteristics to both Israel and Philistia.

▣ "the ark of the covenant of the Lord" The ark symbolized YHWH's
personal presence. They thought its presence would assure victory (cf. Num. 10:35-36 and possibly Josh. 3:10-11).
Also see note on p. 286 of IVP Bible Background Commentary.

SPECIAL TOPIC: ARK OF THE COVENANT

verses.zh: 于是百姓打发人到示罗，从那里将坐在二基路伯上万军之耶和华的约柜抬来。以利的两个儿子何弗尼、非尼哈与　神的约柜同来。
verses.en: So the army[NOTE:1] sent to Shiloh, and they took from there the ark of the covenant of the Lord of Heaven’s Armies, who sits between the cherubim. Now the two sons of Eli, Hophni and Phinehas, were there with the ark of the covenant of God.
notes: Or “people.”
verses.commentary:
4:4 "the Lord of hosts" See

SPECIAL TOPIC: Lord OF HOSTS.

▣ "the cherubim" See
SPECIAL TOPIC: CHERUBIM.

▣ "the ark of the covenant of God" Notice how "YHWH" (v. 3) and "Elohim" (v. 4) are parallel.

SPECIAL TOPIC: NAMES FOR DEITY, C. and D.

verses.zh: 耶和华的约柜到了营中，以色列众人就大声欢呼，地便震动。
verses.en: When the ark of the covenant of the Lord arrived at the camp, all Israel shouted so loudly[NOTE:1] that the ground shook.
notes: Heb “shouted [with] a great shout.”
verses.commentary:
4:5 "so that the earth resounded" This is an obvious hyperbole. However, it was really loud and it scared
the Philistines (vv. 6-8).

verses.zh: 非利士人听见欢呼的声音，就说：「在希伯来人营里大声欢呼，是甚么缘故呢？」随后就知道耶和华的约柜到了营中。
verses.en: When the Philistines heard the sound of the shout, they said, “What is this loud shout in the camp of the Hebrews?” Then they realized that the ark of the Lord had arrived at the camp.

verses.zh: 非利士人就惧怕起来，说：「有神到了他们营中」；又说：「我们有祸了！向来不曾有这样的事。
verses.en: The Philistines were scared because they thought that gods had come to the camp.[NOTE:1] They said, “Woe to us! We’ve never seen anything like this!
notes: The Hebrew text has a direct quote, “because they said, ‘Gods have come to the camp.’” Even though the verb translated “have come” is singular, the following subject should be taken as plural (“gods”), as v. 8 indicates. Some emend the verb to a plural form.
verses.commentary:
4:7-8 "God has come into the camp" This is the term Elohim used in v. 4. It is
plural. It can mean
"in the mouth of these pagans."

- Israel's covenant God ‒ NASB, NKJV, NJB, JPSOA, Peshitta (the verb is singular which usually means
Elohim refers to YHWH)

- a god ‒ TEV, REB, RSV

- gods (v. 8) ‒ NRSV, NET

- the gods ‒ LXX

Verse 8 clarifies that it was the Hebrew God who delivered them from Egyptian bondage, who
has now entered the camp of the Israelites!

verses.zh: 我们有祸了！谁能救我们脱离这些大能之神的手呢？从前在旷野用各样灾殃击打埃及人的，就是这些神。
verses.en: Woe to us! Who can deliver us from the hand of these mighty gods? These are the gods who struck the Egyptians with all sorts of plagues in the desert!

verses.zh: 非利士人哪，你们要刚强，要作大丈夫，免得作希伯来人的奴仆，如同他们作你们的奴仆一样。你们要作大丈夫，与他们争战。」
verses.en: Be strong and act like men, you Philistines, or else you will wind up serving the Hebrews the way they have served you! Act like men and fight!”

verses.zh: 非利士人和以色列人打仗，以色列人败了，各向各家奔逃，被杀的人甚多，以色列的步兵仆倒了三万。
verses.en: So the Philistines fought. Israel was defeated; they all ran home.[NOTE:1] The slaughter was very great; 30,000 foot soldiers from Israel fell in battle.
notes: Heb “and they fled, each to his tents.”
verses.commentary:
4:10 "thirty-thousand foot soldiers" The number "thousand" had seven connotations (i.e., Jdgs. 20:2).

SPECIAL TOPIC: THOUSAND (eleph)

verses.zh: 神的约柜被掳去，以利的两个儿子何弗尼、非尼哈也都被杀了。
verses.en: The ark of God was taken, and the two sons of Eli, Hophni and Phinehas, were killed.

verses.zh: 当日，有一个便雅悯人从阵上逃跑，衣服撕裂，头蒙灰尘，来到示罗。
verses.en: On that day[NOTE:1] a Benjaminite ran from the battle lines and came to Shiloh. His clothes were torn, and dirt was on his head.
notes: Or perhaps, “the same day.” On this use of the demonstrative pronoun see Joüon 2:532 §143.f.
verses.commentary:
4:12 "a man of Benjamin ran" The ANE used trained long-distance runners to carry messages (i.e., 2 Sam. 18:19).

▣ "clothes torn and dust on his head" See

SPECIAL TOPIC: GRIEVING RITES.

verses.zh: 到了的时候，以利正在道旁坐在自己的位上观望，为　神的约柜心里担忧。那人进城报信，合城的人就都呼喊起来。
verses.en: When he arrived in Shiloh, Eli was sitting in his chair on the lookout[NOTE:1] by the side of[NOTE:2] the road, for he was very worried[NOTE:3] about the ark of God. As the man entered the city to give his report,[NOTE:4] the whole city cried out.
notes: The Qal of this verb, צָפָה (tsafah), means “to look.” (The more common word for “to see” is רָאָה, raʾah). Here the ptc. is Piel, which means “to be on the lookout for, look” (HALOT 1045 s.v. I צָפָה). Since we are told later that Eli could not see (which may mean that his eyesight was poor), the important part of using this verb is that Eli positioned himself to get the news as soon as it arrived.
Read with many medieval Hebrew mss, the Qere, and much versional evidence יַד (yad, “hand”) rather than MT יַךְ (yakh).
Heb “his heart was trembling.”
Heb “and the man came to report in the city.”
verses.commentary:
4:13 "Eli was sitting on his seat" Verse 18 implies to me that the seat was on top of a wall overlooking
the tabernacle enclosure. But this is just speculation on my part, although Josephus (Antiq. 5.11.3) calls it "a high throne
at one of the gates."

verses.zh: 以利听见呼喊的声音就问说：「这喧嚷是甚么缘故呢？」那人急忙来报信给以利。
verses.en: When Eli heard the outcry,[NOTE:1] he said, “What’s this commotion?”[NOTE:2] The man quickly came and told Eli.
notes: Heb “the sound of the cry.”
Heb “the sound of this commotion.”

verses.zh: 那时以利九十八岁了，眼目发直，不能看见。
verses.en: Now Eli was ninety-eight years old and his eyes looked straight ahead;[NOTE:1] he was unable to see.
notes: Heb “were set” or “were fixed,” i.e., without vision.
verses.commentary: 4:15 "ninety-eight years old" This is a very specific number. It is obviously an eye-witness or recorded detail.

verses.zh: 那人对以利说：「我是从阵上来的，今日我从阵上逃回。」以利说：「我儿，事情怎样？」
verses.en: The man said to Eli, “I am the one who came from the battle lines! Just today I fled from the battle lines!” Eli[NOTE:1] asked, “How did things go, my son?”
notes: Heb “he”; the referent (Eli) has been specified in the translation for clarity.

verses.zh: 报信的回答说：「以色列人在非利士人面前逃跑，民中被杀的甚多！你的两个儿子何弗尼、非尼哈也都死了，并且　神的约柜被掳去。」
verses.en: The messenger replied, “Israel has fled from[NOTE:1] the Philistines! The army has suffered a great defeat! Your two sons, Hophni and Phinehas, are dead! The ark of God has been captured!”
notes: Heb “before.”

verses.zh: 他一提　神的约柜，以利就从他的位上往后跌倒，在门旁折断颈项而死；因为他年纪老迈，身体沉重。以利作以色列的士师四十年。
verses.en: When he mentioned the ark of God, Eli[NOTE:1] fell backward from his chair beside the gate. He broke his neck and died, for he[NOTE:2] was old and heavy. He had judged Israel for 40 years.
notes: Heb “he”; the referent (Eli) has been specified in the translation for clarity.
Heb “the man.”
verses.commentary:
4:18 "he judged" The term "judge" comes from the Hebrew VERB shophetim (BDB 1047,
KB 1622, Qal ACTIVE PARTICIPLE), which meant "to settle a dispute." This Hebrew term is similar
to (R. K. Harrison, Introduction to the Old Testament, p. 680):

- the Canaanite term for "leader" or "prince" (cf. Amos 2:3)

- the Phoenician term for "regent"

- the Akkadian term for "ruler"

- the Carthaginean term, "chief magistrate"

▣ "Israel" See
SPECIAL TOPIC: ISRAEL (THE NAME).

▣ "forty years" See
SPECIAL TOPIC: SYMBOLIC NUMBERS IN SCRIPTURE, #7.

verses.zh: 以利的儿妇、非尼哈的妻怀孕将到产期，她听见　神的约柜被掳去，公公和丈夫都死了，就猛然疼痛，曲身生产；
verses.en: His daughter-in-law, the wife of Phinehas, was pregnant and close to giving birth. When she heard that the ark of God was captured and that her father-in-law and her husband were dead, she doubled over and gave birth. But her labor pains were too much for her.

verses.zh: 将要死的时候，旁边站着的妇人们对她说：「不要怕！你生了男孩子了。」她却不回答，也不放在心上。
verses.en: As she was dying, the women who were there with her said, “Don’t be afraid! You have given birth to a son!” But she did not reply or pay any attention.[NOTE:1]
notes: Heb “and she did not set her heart.”

verses.zh: 她给孩子起名叫以迦博，说：「荣耀离开以色列了！」这是因　神的约柜被掳去，又因她公公和丈夫都死了。
verses.en: She named the boy Ichabod,[NOTE:1] saying, “The glory has departed from Israel,” referring to the capture of the ark of God and the deaths of her father-in-law and her husband.
notes: The name Ichabod (אִי־כָבוֹד) may mean, “Where is the glory?”
verses.commentary:
4:21 "Ichabod" The name (BDB 33) is defined as "the glory has departed." It refers to the ark being captured
by the Philistines (v. 22).

The Hebrew אי (BDB 33,
which are the first two letters of the name "Ichabod") can mean

- "where" (Rotherham, או)

- "alas" (BDB 33 III)

- "no, not" (BDB IV, "no glory")

- "disgrace" (Josephus, Antiq. 5.11.4)

These discussion questions are provided to help you think through the major issues of this section of
the book. They are meant to be thought-provoking, not definitive.

- Why was Israel's defeat seen as YHWH's doing? (v. 3)

- Define "the Lord of hosts."

- Why were the Philistines fearful of the ark?

- Define "Ichabod."

- Why do some think the "tent of meeting" and "the ark of the covenant" were separated in 1 Samuel 4-7?

WORD AND PHRASE STUDY

NASB (UPDATED) TEXT: 4:1-4

1Thus the word of Samuel came to all Israel. Now Israel went out to meet the Philistines in battle and camped
beside Ebenezer while the Philistines camped in Aphek. 2The Philistines drew up in battle array to meet Israel.
When the battle spread, Israel was defeated before the Philistines who killed about four thousand men on the battlefield.
3When the people came into the camp, the elders of Israel said, "Why has the Lord
defeated us today before the Philistines? Let us take to ourselves from Shiloh the ark of the covenant of the
Lord, that it may come among us and deliver us from the power of our enemies."
4So the people sent to Shiloh, and from there they carried the ark of the covenant of the
Lord of hosts who sits above the cherubim; and the two sons of Eli, Hophni and Phinehas,
were there with the ark of the covenant of God.
